caseno: Appeal From Original Order No.199 of 1996
lawyer:
Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, with Abdus Salam Khan, Advocates—For the Appellants 
Mahmudul Islam, Advocate —For the Respondents
parties:
Dr. Ismat Mirza and others ----- Appellants
Vs.
Md. Mosaddique Hossain  and others ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md. Gholam Rabbani J: This appeal arises out of a pre-emption case under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. Necessary facts for the disposal of this appeal are undisputed and are as follows: 

 3. On the prayer of the preempted under Order 14, rule 2, CPC, trial Court framed and considered the issues of law. By the judgment and order dated 6-11-96 trial Court held that the preemption case was not maintainable in law as barred under section 85(2) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and dismissed the case. Trial Court relied upon a decision reported in 33 DLR 10 and observed that the decision reported in 17 DLR 384 was not applicable in the instant case. 

 4. Mr. Khondokar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the appellant, submits that the trial Court misunderstood section 85(2) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and failed to notice that the right of preemption provided under section 24 of the Act has not been taken away by section 85(2) as held by a Full Bench decision reported in 17 DLR 384. Learned Advocate further submits that the decision in 33 DLR 10 is not applicable in this case wherein the land sought to be preempted was the government Khas land meant for settlement on temporary basis. 

 5. In reply Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate for the respondent, submits that there is no scope for holding otherwise than that the preemption case is not maintainable even if section 85(2) is simply read Learned Advocate submits that the language of the section is plain and admits nolie but one meaning as understood by the trial Court. Besides relying upon 33 DLR 10, he reads an observation, "The scheme of the Act also shows that the legislature only meant to exclude such land from operation of this Act which was held by the tenant directly under the government" from a decision reported in 7 DLR 116. Mr. Islam further submits that if section 85(2) is read along with section 81A of the SA & T Act then it will be clear that the provisions of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act are not applicable to a non-agricultural tenant who has not become tenant under the Government due to acquisition of rent-receiving interest of his landlord. 

 6. Section 81A of the SA & T Act runs as follows " "(I) Except as otherwise provided in this Part, the rights and liabilities of a holder of non-agricultural land, who has become a tenant under the Government in respect of such land by virtue of the acquisition of the superior right in such land under the provisions of this Act, shall, where the provisions of the East Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949, (EB Act XXIII of 1949) applied to such land, at the time of such acquisition, be regulated by the provisions of that Act. (2) The rights and liabilities of other non-agricultural tenants shall, except in the matter of determination, enhancement or reduction of rent, be governed by the terms of the lease and the provisions of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Act IV of 1882): (Proviso is omitted). 

 7. Section 85(2) of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act runs as follows: "Nothing in this Act shall apply to any non-agricultural land held by a tenant under the Government: 

 9. The puzzle word is "tenant". What section 85(2) means by the word "tenant" contained in it? "Tenant" ordinarily means an occupier of immovable property paying rent to a persons who is generally called "landlord". This definition in not sufficient There are two categories of tenants. One has the full ownership in the land i.e. it is transferable and heritable and the other has not. Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act was enacted for the first category and not for the second category. Section 85(2) speaks about the second category. If this section wanted to mean the first category, then it would have used the expression "non-agricultural tenant" instead of the word "tenant". 

 13. In view of our discussion as above, we hold that an application under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act in respect of the land situated within Dhanmondi Residential Area is maintainable. Decision of the Single Bench in 33 DLR 10 is not a correct decision and is overruled. Other decisions cited by the learned Advocates are not relevant in this matter.
